3. The petitioner who is facing trial for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and under Sections 4 and 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Section 9 of the Child Marriage Act is before this Court seeking relief.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. The prosecution alleging that the petitioner - accused fully aware that the respondent No.2 survivor is a minor kidnapped her and had committed forcible sexual intercourse.

5. The petitioner-accused and respondent No.2 are present before this Court and have filed a joint NC: 2025:KHC:10013 affidavit stating that the sexual intercourse between them was consensual, as they were in a relationship.

6. The survivor as of the date of incident was 17 years 1 month, and as of today is 19 years and their marriage was solemnized on 13.05.2024 and the same was registered on 25.02.2025 in the office of Sub- Registrar, Kengeri.
7. The survivor further stated that from the said wedlock, a female child was born who is approximately one and a half months old as of today.

She added that if the petitioner is subjected to Sri Darshan vs State Of Karnataka on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64282066/
2 trial, it would likely result in incarceration, causing more misery and agony rather than securing the ends of justice.

entities.text: Sri Darshan vs State Of Karnataka on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, she stated that she and her daughter are solely dependent on the accused for their daily needs.

8. The object of POCSO Act is to protect minors form sexual abuse and not to criminalize the consensual relationship between two adolescents who had consensual sexual intercourse without knowing the consequences.

The petitioner and the survivor come from the lower socio economic segment having limited access to information and knowledge, thus depriving them of the consequences in having consensual sexual intercourse.

Though having sexual intercourse consensually with the minor is an NC: 2025:KHC:10013 offence under the POCSO Act, however,
having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, to secure the ends of justice, it would be appropriate to quash the impugned proceedings, otherwise, it would result in miscarriage of justice to the survivor.
9. In the light of the forgoing discussion, it would be an abuse of process of law that the criminal proceedings are allowed to continue.

10. Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.
 (ii) The impugned proceedings in  Spl.C.C.No.545/2023 on the file of the  Additional District and Sessions, FTSC-II,
Bangalore Rural District, Bengaluru is hereby quashed.
(iii) The bail bond if any, stands discharged.

Sd/-
